concepts_present.evidence_quote: We propose a novel loss we term the Focal Loss that focuses training on a sparse set of hard examples and prevents the vast number of easy negatives from overwhelming the detector.
We design and train a simple dense detector we call RetinaNet ... matches the speed of previous one-stage detectors.
RetinaNet uses translation-invariant anchor boxes ... 9 anchors per location ... 3 scales x 3 aspect ratios.
RetinaNet uses a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) backbone on top of a feedforward ResNet architecture.
Our best model, RetinaNet with ResNet-101-FPN ...
Box predictions ... are then thresholded ... and decoded into the final detections via NMS.
All ablation experiments use ResNet-50-FPN ... on COCO trainval35k.

concepts_absent.rationale: RetinaNet is a one-stage dense detector; no region-proposal stage.
RetinaNet is anchor-based; the anchor-free narrative emerges later (FCOS, ATSS).
RetinaNet relies on NMS, not bipartite matching.
Architecture is fully convolutional FPN; no transformer.
Compound scaling is later EfficientDet; RetinaNet primarily varies depth/backbone.
